title: Scheduler priority fairness regression — emergency follow-up
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After a prioritized scheduler heuristic change deployed in runtime-1.28, we observed a sustained p95/p99 latency regression for small-sequence, low-token-count requests across several hosted clusters. The regression began ~2026-02-17 03:10 UTC after a staging-promoted change that altered request priority scoring and batch preemption thresholds. Impact: production customer-facing latency SLOs were violated for 62 hours in affected regions, resulting in increased error budgets and several customer support escalations. Scope: primarily small inference requests (<= 64 tokens) that would previously be routed to the fast-path kernel; these requests experienced queuing delays caused by scheduler inflating batch assembly time and delaying KV cache warmups.
timeline: 2026-02-17 02:45 UTC — Rollout of scheduler priority heuristic PR #1418 promoted from staging to canary on us-west-2 clusters.
2026-02-17 03:10 UTC — Canary telemetry shows p95 increase for small-seq paths; pager triggered for increase > 50ms.
2026-02-17 04:00 UTC — Automatic rollout paused; initial mitigation toggles applied to revert new preemption thresholds on canary nodes.
2026-02-17 07:30 UTC — Full rollback of heuristic performed to runtime-1.27 configuration across affected region clusters.
2026-02-17 08:00 UTC — Latency returned close to baseline on most clusters; continued elevated tail observed on mixed-quant pools.
2026-02-18 10:00 UTC — Begin deeper investigation: reproduce locally with synthetic small-sequence workload and representative model kernels.

2026-02-19 14:20 UTC — Root-cause hypothesis refined: priority score change combined with longer batch assembly window caused high-priority small requests to be queued behind preempting medium batches; KV cache miss rates increased for reprioritized paths.
2026-02-20 09:00 UTC — Hotfix PR #1426 deployed: tuned scoring coefficients, reduced batch-assembly timeout for fast-path lanes, added short-circuit for known warm KV-cache handles.
2026-02-20 10:30 UTC — Hotfix validated against synthetic workload; production rollout phased over 2 hours. Tail latency reduced to target in majority of pools.
2026-02-26 16:00 UTC — This follow-up ticket opened to track long-term actions and ensure automation/regression coverage.
findings: The scheduler heuristic change (PR #1418) adjusted the priority scoring vector to favor throughput for medium-length sequences; this unintentionally reduced priority weight for tiny requests resulting in increased batch wait time.
A longer 'batch assembly window' intended to increase packing efficiency amplified queuing for small requests, causing them to miss fast-path kernel dispatch opportunities.
KV cache warmup relied on fast dispatch; when small requests were delayed they often missed existing warm handles and suffered cache-miss penalties when finally scheduled.
Mixed-quant GPU pools exhibited higher residual tail due to kernel selection probes that are more expensive when requests are delayed and arrive with stale KV state.
Canary rollout instrumentation did not highlight the small-sequence tail because canary traffic mix was skewed toward medium sequences; gating tests lacked a small-sequence heavy synthetic scenario.
Alert thresholds were set on overall p95 but not on per-route / per-sequence-length buckets, delaying detection of the regression surface.
mitigations: Immediate rollback to runtime-1.27 heuristic was performed during incident to stop the regression.
Hotfix PR #1426 adjusted scoring coefficients and introduced a sub-ms short-circuit for confirmed warm KV handles to favor fast-path dispatch for <=64 token requests.
Added temporary autoscaling rule to burst additional fast-path capacity for affected pools during peak periods while long-term fixes are implemented.
Instrumented per-sequence-length histograms and per-model-route latency alerts so future regressions are visible at the granular level they manifest.
Added a small-sequence heavy canary scenario to the deployment pipeline to validate future scheduler changes.
action_items: ENG: Add deterministic unit and integration tests that simulate small-sequence traffic under various packing windows — owner: Marco Villanueva — ETA: 2026-03-05
ENG/R&D: Revisit scoring vector design and publish a short design note with rationale and safety bounds — owner: Priya Rao — ETA: 2026-03-12
Infra: Create per-route, per-sequence-length alerting dashboard panels and set p95/p99 alarms — owner: Jordan Li — ETA: 2026-03-01
QA: Add small-sequence heavy canary test to CI pipeline (both synthetic & replay) and require green for scheduler heuristic changes — owner: Mei Chen — ETA: 2026-03-08
SRE: Bake an automated rollback runbook that triggers when small-sequence p99 exceeds baseline by > 30% for 15 minutes — owner: Carlos Ramos — ETA: 2026-03-03
Product: Communicate incident summary and customer impact to affected accounts with recommended mitigations and ETA for full fix — owner: Lila Morgan — ETA: 2026-02-28
EngOps: Add regression benchmark (microbench) to performance gate that runs during deploys to canary and release pipelines — owner: Nikhil Gupta — ETA: 2026-03-10
Research: Evaluate adaptive batch-assembly windows that shrink for fast-path lanes under detected small-seq load — owner: Dr. Elena Kovacs — ETA: 2026-04-02
notes: Related: see ENG-421007 for previous probe/quarantine work that influenced the preemption model; ensure there is no semantic overlap when revising scoring.
Consider adding a lightweight 'fast-path only' queue for ultra-low-latency requests as a long-term robustness measure; cost analysis required.

We intentionally left security_review_required=false because this change is operational and does not affect customer data handling, but security should be notified if any telemetry changes are proposed.
Follow-up retrospective meeting scheduled 2026-03-02 16:00 UTC with Engineering, SRE, Product, and QA to review progress on action items and close ticket.
